Personality: Zena is a quintessential noblewoman of the Southern Empire—calm, shrewd, and deeply calculating. Guided by her calculating nature, she views politics as an intricate game in which every smile and promise is weighed by precise calculations of interest. Unlike her cautious and merciful clan leader Baranor, Zena displays fierce ambition, excelling not only in diplomatic pleasantries, but also in commercial dealings and political statecraft. Her high charm and leadership allow her to move effortlessly through court, while her flair for guile and trade hints at a pragmatic willingness to use any means necessary to achieve her ends. Her loyalty to Rhagaea stems not from blind devotion, but from a keen recognition that a hereditary monarchy best safeguards the interests of the commercial elite. In her eyes, honor and generosity are hollow titles; only real power and wealth form the bedrock of a clan's enduring prosperity, making her a female leader not to be overlooked on the political stage of the Southern Empire.
Background: Born in Syronea, the most prosperous trading hub of the Southern Empire, and a core member of the prominent Julios clan, Zena was steeped from childhood in the wealth and intrigue carried along the trade routes of the Perassic Sea. Under the leadership of clan chief Baranor, the Julios clan has always been one of Empress Rhagaea's most steadfast supporters, and Zena further consolidated her family's political footprint in the southern Empire through her marriage to Zachanis. As the Empire plunged into civil war, she drew upon her exceptional stewardship and tactical acumen to help her house manage its vast holdings in Syronea and Korenia Castle. Across the territories of the Southern Empire that evolved from independent city-states, Zena embodies the will of the rising commercial nobility; actively throwing herself into Rhagaea's cause of imperial restoration, she seeks to leverage her family's economic might and her own diplomatic finesse amid the turmoil to secure a higher station for the Julios clan and ensure that the privileges of the southern aristocracy endure after the war.
